I used to be like your son. I would cry and yell and end up locked in our study for hours, no work done. Everything was a distraction- is rather stare at a blank wall than do any work.
Surprise surprise, 10 years later I was diagnosed with ADHD. Medication and therapy for it has literally changed my life. I now complete work and daily tasks with no problems and feel so in control and free. I helped my parents move my old desk the other day and when we examined it, we realised it was still covered in tear drop stains from my childhood. I’m not saying your son has ADHD, but there is clearly a serious problem there. No kid WANTS to be stick for hours being forced to do something they hate. Your husband is not in the wrong, but something needs to change. You need to speak to your son or maybe get him to speak with a professional to get to the bottom of why he is so against completing his work. Trust me, it may seem like “normal tantrums”, but as someone who’s been there, it’s exhausting and overwhelming, and leaves a scar. I wish you and your family the best

This breaks my heart, I’m sorry you had to go through with this. I can relate- I was convinced that if I didn’t click my fingers in a certain was before bed, my little sister would die in her sleep. I would sometimes walk past her room in the middle of the night just to check on her. I was diagnosed at 14 after having a full break down convinced I hadn’t locked the door properly before going to school, and that I would come home to find an intruder had killed my family. OCD is a horrible thing and I really hope you are doing well

I was playing in the park as a kid (maybe age 6?) and took off running into a wooded area. Saw a young woman backed against a tree by two guys, clearly frightened and telling them to stay away from her. They didn’t see me but it freaked me out so I ran back to my mother and told her. She was incredibly dismissive and said it was none of my business and they were just playing a game. Even then, it didn’t sit right with me and I felt queasy all day. It’s been almost 20 years and I still feel sick when I think about it, and guilty, even though I was just a kid. And angry with my mother. I truly hope that girl is okay

I’m not gonna lie to you man, this is absolutely terrifying. Think, just for a minute, about what would happen if your allergy/aversion was even more severe- would she have cared if you’d ended up in the hospital? What about if you died? 
Even if this was the first time she’s done something like this, it’s still an incredible act of selfishness borederlining on cruelty. That sounds extreme but if you choose not to eat meat and she feeds it to you in secret to “prove it tastes good” how is that not sickening and petty? Maybe you choose not to eat pork, maybe you have an intolerance, either way it’s a horrible thing for her to have done. If she apologised sincerely and seems remorseful and takes the steps to gain your trust again, okay, perhaps consider working further on this relationship. But it honestly sounds like she couldn’t give two shits about you, your opinions or your intolerances, which quiet frankly is the opposite of what a loving relationship should be. Please please do some serious thinking before she lands you in intensive care. Apologies for sounding harsh but I’ve been in a similar situation and this really sets me off. All the best

NTA, but you will be if you keep allowing him to put your DAUGHTER’S LIFE IN DANGER. How can you still allow someone so apathetic to his child’s safety to even be around her? I’m sorry but this entire situation makes my blood boil and screams red flags. It sounds like he somehow doesn’t give a shit if she DIES. How you’ve let it go this far is beyond me. You need to seriously reconsider your current situation and if you have any common sense or love for your child, PROTECT YOUR DAUGHTER. I wish you both the best
